step1_analysis.description: A complementary cross-coupled LC-VCO core with both PMOS and NMOS cross-coupled pairs for negative resistance. It includes PMOS and NMOS accumulation/inversion varactors for differential frequency tuning.

paper_reference.title: A Subpicosecond Jitter PLL for Clock Generation in 0.12-m Digital CMOS

oscillation_frequency.description: The fundamental operating frequency of the oscillator.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the added tank inductance (5nH) and the total parasitic/varactor capacitance. f = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L * C)).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Since the inductors were external to the netlist, a 5nH inductor was added in the testbench. The frequency will depend on this L and the varactor C at 0.9V tuning.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the VCO core from the supply.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * I_tail. With VDD=1.8V and a tail current limited by transistor headroom to ~0.5-2mA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper reports 35mW for the entire PLL. The VCO core alone typically consumes a small fraction of the total PLL power.

sky130_expected.calculation: V_swing = I_tail * R_tank. With an ideal inductor, the swing is limited by the supply voltage and transistor saturation headroom.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper mentions 300mV for CML dividers, so the VCO must output at least this much to drive them properly.

phase_noise.description: Single sideband phase noise at 1-MHz offset from the carrier.

sky130_expected.calculation: Estimated via Leeson's equation based on tank Q, oscillation frequency, and active device noise.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Highly dependent on the Q-factor of the physical inductors used, which are idealized in this standard transient testbench.

step3_testbench.description: Transient testbench to verify oscillation, measure frequency, power consumption, and differential voltage swing. An ideal tank inductor is added to enable oscillation.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Subpicosecond Jitter PLL VCO Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u
.param W_xm8=5u L_xm8=0.5u
.param W_xm9=5u L_xm9=0.5u
.param W_xm10=5u L_xm10=0.5u

XM1 TUNEP OUTQ TUNEP VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 OUT OUTQ N3 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 OUT OUTQ VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 TUNEP OUT TUNEP VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 BIAS BIAS VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 OUTQ OUT N3 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM7 N3 BIAS VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}
XM8 OUTQ OUT VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm8} w={W_xm8}
XM9 TUNEN OUTQ TUNEN VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm9} w={W_xm9}
XM10 TUNEN OUT TUNEN VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm10} w={W_xm10}

* Power and Bias Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVSS VSS 0 0
Ibias VDD BIAS 2m
VTUNEP TUNEP 0 0.9
VTUNEN TUNEN 0 0.9

* Tank Inductor and Capacitor (added to enable oscillation)
L1 OUT OUTQ 5n
C1 OUT OUTQ 100f

* VCVS to create a single-ended differential voltage node for easy measurement
E1 VDIFF 0 OUT OUTQ 1

* Kickstart current pulse to initiate oscillation without breaking DC operating point
Ikick OUT OUTQ PWL(0 0 1n 1m 1.1n 0)

.control
  tran 10p 30n
  
  * Measure oscillation frequency (time between 5th and 6th zero-crossing)
  meas tran t1 trig v(VDIFF) val=0 rise=5 targ v(VDIFF) val=0 rise=6
  let osc_freq = 1 / t1
  print osc_freq
  
  * Measure power consumption
  meas tran pwr_avg avg i(VVDD) from=10n to=30n
  let power_W = -pwr_avg * 1.8
  print power_W
  
  * Measure output voltage swing (differential peak-to-peak)
  meas tran vmax max v(VDIFF) from=10n to=30n
  meas tran vmin min v(VDIFF) from=10n to=30n
  let vswing_diff = vmax - vmin
  print vswing_diff
  
  quit
.endc
